answer: Each newcomer needs an established patron, and its required stake grows with every name already vetted: the first ward costs one bond, the fifth costs five, so a backer carrying k aliases locks about k-squared times the base. If any ward is exposed, the patron forfeits the whole stake, so a farm cannot rent one busy backer cheaply. It must spread across many patrons, each paying its own climbing schedule. The oasis of casual sponsorship dries up, the kernel of each seat is a distinct underwriter with real exposure, and a bridge to a thousand clones is funded a thousand times over.
